title: Update: my homebrew D&D campaign is now a playable browser RPG. What finally worked for consistent 3D heroes across 39 races
author: OpenToFriends
selftext:
About a month ago I posted here that I was turning my homebrew D&D campaign into a 2.5D RPG. It now has a free demo you can play in the browser: **https://play.thecentralnexus.com/index.html** (desktop, keyboard + mouse).

**What finally worked for the heroes:** I spent weeks trying to get drawn pixel sprites to work for a character creator with 39 races and swappable outfits. Heads and hair never sat right when drawn separately. What worked:

1. One clean 4-view character sheet per race (front, back, two sides), generated from my own designs and the in-game art as the identity reference
2. Image-to-3D (Tripo), then auto-rig + Mixamo animations
3. In Babylon.js: a toon shader + outline, then a low-res "pixel layer" pass at render time, so the 3D model reads as pixel art next to the hand-built world

That made every race consistent and let them all share one animation set. Height per race is set from the 5e size rules, so Dwarves, Gnomes and Halflings actually stand shorter.

**The rest:** the world, story and characters come from my own campaign book; the code was written with AI coding agents, with a separate agent reviewing every change before it was merged.

Happy to answer questions about the pipeline. Feedback form if you try it: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSedSUUoHDxpzbb7Q9eBL6Qp59RrYN3AP5A7uykYnEzFS6hpsQ/viewform
